display.title: Believe in Moshiach: The Rambam's Rule and the Great Shofar
display.summary_short: The Rambam teaches every Jew to believe that Moshiach can come any day; we pray for it in benching and Shemoneh Esrei, and the second horn of Yitzchak's ram waits to announce his arrival.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi introduces the Rambam, about whom it is said that from Moshe to Moshe there arose none like Moshe, and teaches one of his rules: every Jew must truly believe that any day Eliyahu HaNavi may appear with the news that Moshiach has come. We remember this in benching, asking Hashem to send Eliyahu HaNavi with good tidings, and three times a day in Shemoneh Esrei, when we ask Hashem to sound the great shofar of our freedom. He retells the Akeidah: our Sages say Avraham kept both horns of the ram; one was sounded when the Torah was given, and the other will be sounded by Hashem Himself, heard all over the world, when Moshiach comes. Moshiach will be chosen by Hashem just as Moshe Rabbeinu was. This belief has kept the Jewish people alive through every age, because exile is not forever. Now is the time to learn more Torah, do more mitzvos, give more tzedakah and love every Jew, to show Hashem that we have had enough of exile.
display.lesson: Believe that Moshiach can come any day, and bring him sooner with more Torah, mitzvos, tzedakah and Ahavas Yisroel.
